key_insight: An interpretable machine-learning model could predict early Parkinson’s progression to mild cognitive impairment and postural instability using a small set of readily available clinical features, with only limited added benefit from multimodal biomarkers and imaging.
clinical_relevance: If validated, this approach could help stratify early PD patients by risk of cognitive and motor worsening and support more personalized monitoring and planning.
method: Explainable Boosting Machines (EBM) used for prediction in two independent early-PD cohorts.
Compared a minimal clinico-demographic feature set with an extended multimodal set including brain imaging and fluid biomarkers.
Identified baseline age and MoCA total score as the strongest predictors in the minimal model; additional motor, cognitive, and imaging features contributed in the extended model.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports comparable predictive performance between the minimal and extended models across two independent cohorts, suggesting robust signal from standard clinical variables.
watch_item: Performance and generalizability still need external validation before use in real-world clinical decision-making, especially given cohort-specific data and endpoint definitions.
paper_title: Explainable machine learning identifies predictors for postural instability and cognitive impairment in early Parkinsons Disease
